previous_statement: At each level define F_z(X,Y)=v_n(X)z_n(Y)-z_n(XY)+z_n(X)v_n(Y). Expanding g_n and using associativity of M_n tensor B gives the exact cocycle residual v_n(X)g_n(Y,Z)-g_n(XY,Z)+g_n(X,YZ)-g_n(X,Y)v_n(Z), which is the associator (v_n(X)v_n(Y))v_n(Z)-v_n(X)(v_n(Y)v_n(Z)); its norm is at most 2 epsilon||X||||Y||||Z|| for d+epsilon<=1/4. Substituting z=w_prime, using X D=D X entrywise and pi(D)=I, and applying the d-multiplicativity bound at each of the finitely many replacements yields ||F_(w_prime)(X,Y)-g_n(X,Y)||<=C_0(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y||, where C_0 is universal because sum_j||A_j||||B_j||=1.
new_statement: At each level put F_z(X,Y)=v_n(X)z_n(Y)-z_n(XY)+z_n(X)v_n(Y). Expanding g_n and using associativity of M_n tensor B gives v_n(X)g_n(Y,Z)-g_n(XY,Z)+g_n(X,YZ)-g_n(X,Y)v_n(Z)=(v_n(X)v_n(Y))v_n(Z)-v_n(X)(v_n(Y)v_n(Z)), whose norm is at most 2 epsilon||X||||Y||||Z|| when d+epsilon<=1/4. In F_(w_prime), successively replace v_n(X)v_n(I tensor A_j) by v_n(X(I tensor A_j)); use X D=D X under the bilinear map (C,D)->v_n(C)g_n(D,Y); apply the displayed cocycle identity to (I tensor B_j,X,Y); reassociate v_n(I tensor A_j)(v_n(I tensor B_j)g_n(X,Y)); replace the first two factors by v_n(I tensor A_j B_j); sum using pi(D)=I; and replace v_n(I)g_n(X,Y) by g_n(X,Y). The d-multiplicativity, epsilon-associativity, approximate-unit, and product bounds control these seven replacements respectively by fixed multiples of d^2, epsilon*d, epsilon, epsilon*d, d^2, zero, and (d+epsilon)d, each weighted by sum_j||A_j||||B_j||=1. Thus their sum is at most 100(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y||, uniformly in n.
